name: Forgiving Murder
overview: Scripture clearly upholds the sanctity of human life, commanding "Thou shalt not kill" (Exodus 20:13) and prescribing capital punishment for murder as affirmed in Numbers 35:30. The seriousness of shedding innocent blood is underscored by the defilement it brings upon the land, which can only be cleansed by the life of the one who shed it (Numbers 35:33). The Old Testament law also addresses intentional murder with strict consequences (Deuteronomy 19:11; Proverbs 28:17), while Jesus reiterates the gravity of this command in Matthew 5:21, warning that those who kill face judgment. Together, these passages reveal God's just response to murder and the profound need for forgiveness grounded in His holiness and justice.
